concepts.why: The patient's laboratory studies showed hemoglobin 7.3 g/dL, white-cell count 4.0×10^9/L, and platelets 23×10^9/L, and a peripheral-blood smear revealed lymphoblasts, which are characteristic of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
The patient developed febrile neutropenia on day 8, which is a common complication of chemotherapy.
The patient's blood cultures grew Coagulase-negative Staphylococcus species, which is a common cause of infection in neutropenic patients.
The patient's repeat cultures grew Enterococcus species, which is a common cause of infection in neutropenic patients.
The patient reported severe pain in her right arm radiating to her shoulder, suggesting herpes zoster, although no vesicles were present.
The patient's MRI of the right shoulder demonstrated a focal cystic necrotic lesion between the teres minor and teres major muscles, which is consistent with a muscle abscess.
The patient had eczematous plaques on her chest and proximal right arm, which were treated as contact dermatitis with topical methylprednisolone.
The patient had splenomegaly 6 cm below the costal margin, which is a common finding in patients with hematologic malignancies.
The patient's hemoglobin level was 7.3 g/dL, which is consistent with anemia.
The patient's platelet count was 23×10^9/L, which is consistent with thrombocytopenia.
